rule_friction.idea: Merge the two products into one 50x50 product, B·(x_k + γ(x_k − x_{k−1})). The data nearly satisfy D = [−B, B] with B equal to the right half of `t0_state`, which would cut about 6730 multiply-adds per iteration to 2500.
rule_friction.rule: Not blocked by a rule: the relation only holds to about 1e-15, and `t0_state` has tiny (~1e-17) entries in its left half. So the merged routine would not reproduce each member exactly, and I did not risk the per-member verify check.

rule_friction.idea: Build a dense or reordered copy of `t0_state` (or a merged A + γD table) once at setup, in workspace scratch.
rule_friction.rule: `fom_setup` may not probe matrices, and `fom_ops.c` has no setup hook; the alternative is a large literal table, which I tested and was slower

rule_friction.idea: `-ffast-math` or `-march=native` so the compiler can reassociate and use wider vectors on its own.
rule_friction.rule: The Makefile and build flags are fixed

rule_friction.idea: Collapse `A x + g D x` to `B((1+g) x1 - g x0)` with one 50x50 dense block (half the matrix traffic)
rule_friction.rule: the fused/step check must recover each member exactly; the members match only to ~1e-15, so this relation cannot be used safely

rule_friction.idea: Allow `-O3`/`-ffast-math` or `-mcpu` flags so the compiler vectorizes the reductions itself and the hand-written NEON is unnecessary
rule_friction.rule: Makefile and build flags are fixed

rule_friction.idea: Store `A` and `D` interleaved per row tile in one precomputed buffer, built at setup, for better streaming
rule_friction.rule: `fom_setup` may not prepare matrix data, so the lazy static copy inside `fom_step_t0` is the only legal place

rule_friction.idea: Guard the momentum fusion with a runtime check that `d_gamma[:, :50] == -d_gamma[:, 50:]` and `t0_state == [0, d_gamma[:, 50:]]` within a relative tolerance, falling back to the general path otherwise
rule_friction.rule: float-literal rule (the tolerance is not a matrix coefficient, and `fom_step_t0` may only inline the matrix's own values)
rule_friction.expected_gain: none for speed; it adds robustness

rule_friction.idea: Ping-pong the two state halves through pointers so the per-iteration shift memcpy (about 14%) disappears
rule_friction.rule: fixed `fom_step_t0` signature, which takes one contiguous 100-vector state, and headers are not editable

rule_friction.idea: Precompute `A + g_k D` for each scheduled gamma once, which would save forming the momentum point
rule_friction.rule: ops.c may not read the schedule, and setup may not probe or rebuild matrices

rule_friction.idea: Packing W (stride 100) into a contiguous 50x50 table in `fom_setup`
rule_friction.rule: fom_setup cannot read matrix data or call fom_apply; lazily packing inside fom_ops is allowed but L1-resident anyway

rule_friction.idea: Using W's symmetry to cut loads in half (upper triangle with scatter)
rule_friction.rule: none (not blocked; the scatter pattern doesn't vectorize well, so I didn't try it)

rule_friction.idea: Store W in float32 or a precomputed packed layout as static const data in `fom_data.c`, to halve load bandwidth or skip the lazy pack
rule_friction.rule: numeric data and other files are fixed, and precision must stay exact

rule_friction.idea: Fuse the y = x1 + g(x1 - x0) momentum combination and the residual into `fom_iterate`, and run the whole 200-iteration loop inside `src/fom_ops.c` to drop the per-call overhead
rule_friction.rule: `fom_ops.c` may not read the schedule (`fom_sched_*`), so the loop over the gamma schedule must stay in `fom_solver.c`
